name: Daniel Brady, barber

proprietors.name: Daniel Brady
proprietors.basis: ADOPTED, NOT MINTED. Daniel Brady is the reconstructed trade head the resident band's `trade_households` stage drew at barber_surgeon in the south division (slot trade_households:persons/male/20_29/south/family/trade:barber_surgeon:004), and that card says itself that the business band adopts these heads rather than minting its own. Here the head is not merely the proprietor of the house — the head IS what bought it, because no count of this class was ever printed to be short of.

locations.basis: A FACE, NOT A PREMISES. The placement rule for a barber's shop kept by a south-division household deals this house onto Dearborn Street; the face is drawn on the seed printed in `reconstruction.seed` from the faces that rule allows, and no lot, roof or coordinate is claimed. T-1195 writes the placement policy with its evidence and T-1199 seats this house on the lot grid.
locations.limit_reason: No source places this house, because no source names it: it exists because the resident band drew a barber surgeon the town was short of, and the trade names the house he keeps. The street is the reconstruction's own deal and stops there.

dates.basis: NOTHING DATES THIS HOUSE. The head who keeps it is ordered onto the scene date and to nothing narrower, and a keeping is not an opening; the record claims that the house was trading on 1835-07-01 and nothing about either end.

proprietor_community.basis: The 1 keeper(s) this record names and the resident layer holds a card for all read irish: Daniel Brady (irish). A house is not its keeper, so the reading is an inference about the house and is capped there.

replaceable_by: A register, directory or deed naming a real barber's shop in the south division in 1835 — that house takes this slot and this record is withdrawn with the head.

trade_head.note: A TRADE HEAD, NOT A SHORTFALL AND NOT A ROOF. The December 1835 State census's eighteen lines never reach this class, so the order book holds no bucket to point at and no count of it can be short; and nothing in data/structures/ is a barber's shop, so there is no committed building to buy the firm either. What IS committed is the man: the resident band drew Daniel Brady at barber surgeon because the 1839 trade table says the town was short of the trade, and a barber keeps a shop front — PUBLIC_TRADES `shop` of the signage rule — and this project already stands one of them, rcb_fb_barbers_shop, on T-1377's documented floor of the town's free Black residents; that floor is an argument about PEOPLE and it orders no second shop, so the second shop is bought by the head or not at all. The house is withdrawn with the head.

basis.note: the resident band drew 1 head(s) at barber surgeon in the south division and a barber keeps a shop front — PUBLIC_TRADES `shop` of the signage rule — and this project already stands one of them, rcb_fb_barbers_shop, on T-1377's documented floor of the town's free Black residents; that floor is an argument about PEOPLE and it orders no second shop, so the second shop is bought by the head or not at all. The style is dealt on the seed printed beside it from the period forms the register itself carries: THE TRADE HAS NO PRINTING IN THIS CORPUS and no form is composed for it: this is the naming guide's form 1 with the forename in full, and it is the form the project's one standing barber's shop already takes — 'Benjamin Anderson, barber' (rcb_fb_barbers_shop, T-1377). The goods line is the one trade word this project already stands a barber's shop under, and no second line is dealt: the register prints none for the trade, and the naming guide refuses a goods line composed for a class rather than taken from it.

reconstruction.withdrawn_if: the retirement of the head himself, a re-cut of the order book that no longer orders his person bucket, or a source naming a real house of this class; the retirement runs through --build, never by hand
